Dynamic matrices let the student choose one or both dimensions. Use
`mat{...}` only with `mode: custom`; the checker receives each named input as a
SymPy matrix at `response["inputs"][name]["matrix"]`.

::: {.callout-tip}
The controls never infer a dimension from the answer. Authors set neutral
initial dimensions and mathematical bounds. Removing the final row or column
produces the single canonical empty matrix.
:::

::: {#dynamic-matrix-method .math-exercise-context}

A nonempty matrix with $r$ rows and $c$ columns has shape $r\times c$. A
matrix without entries is the empty matrix. For a matrix $A$ with $n$ columns,
a null-space basis matrix $Z$ must satisfy $AZ=0$, have linearly
independent columns, and have $n-\operatorname{rank}(A)$ columns. A set of
points on $y=2x$ consists of distinct row pairs $(x,2x)$. A zero matrix has
only zero entries, regardless of its rectangular shape.

:::

## 1. Choose the number of basis vectors

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-nullspace-basis
#| caption: A basis without announcing nullity
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       Z = response["inputs"]["Z"]["matrix"]
#|       C = Matrix([[1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6]])
#|       valid_columns = [
#|           Z[:, j] != zeros(Z.rows, 1) and C * Z[:, j] == zeros(C.rows, 1)
#|           for j in range(Z.cols)
#|       ]
#|       contained = all(valid_columns)
#|       independent = Z.rank() == Z.cols
#|       complete = Z.cols == C.cols - C.rank()
#|       score = (int(contained) + int(independent) + int(complete)) / 3
#|       return {
#|           "score": score,
#|           "feedback": "Check that every column is a nonzero null-space vector, that the columns are independent, and that the basis is complete.",
#|           "assessment": {"Z": {"columns": valid_columns}}
#|       }

Give a basis for the null space of
$C=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&6\end{bmatrix}$. Enter the basis vectors as
columns of $Z$:

$Z=$ mat{name=Z, rows=3, cols=auto, initial-cols=1, min-cols=0, max-cols=3}
```

## 2. Choose the number of rows

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-point-rows
#| caption: A variable-length list of points
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       P = response["inputs"]["P"]["matrix"]
#|       on_line = all(simplify(P[i, 1] - 2*P[i, 0]) == 0 for i in range(P.rows))
#|       distinct = len({tuple(P.row(i)) for i in range(P.rows)}) == P.rows
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(on_line) + int(distinct)) / 2,
#|           "feedback": "Each row must be a point on y=2x, and the submitted points must be distinct."
#|       }

Give between two and four distinct points on the line $y=2x$, one point per
row:

$P=$ mat{name=P, rows=auto, cols=2, initial-rows=2, min-rows=2, max-rows=4}
```

## 3. Choose both dimensions

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-both-dimensions
#| caption: Any non-square zero matrix
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       A = response["inputs"]["A"]["matrix"]
#|       non_square = A.rows != A.cols
#|       zero = A == zeros(A.rows, A.cols)
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(non_square) + int(zero)) / 2,
#|           "feedback": "The matrix must be rectangular rather than square, and every entry must be zero."
#|       }

Give any non-square zero matrix with at least one row and one column:

$A=$ mat{name=A, rows=auto, cols=auto, initial-rows=2, initial-cols=1, min-rows=1, max-rows=4, min-cols=1, max-cols=4}
```

## 4. The empty basis

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-zero-columns
#| caption: The null-space basis of an invertible matrix
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       Z = response["inputs"]["Z0"]["matrix"]
#|       return {
#|           "correct": Z.rows == 0 and Z.cols == 0,
#|           "feedback": "The null space is trivial, so its basis is empty."
#|       }

Give a basis for the null space of $I_2$. Enter basis vectors as columns:

$Z_0=$ mat{name=Z0, rows=2, cols=auto, initial-cols=1, min-cols=0, max-cols=2}
```

## 5. Empty by removing rows

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-zero-rows
#| caption: The canonical empty state
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       T = response["inputs"]["T"]["matrix"]
#|       return {
#|           "correct": T.rows == 0 and T.cols == 0,
#|           "feedback": "Remove every row to submit the empty matrix."
#|       }

Use the row control to submit the empty matrix:

$T=$ mat{name=T, rows=auto, cols=2, initial-rows=1, min-rows=0, max-rows=3}
```

## 6. A column-space basis

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-column-space-basis
#| caption: Compute a basis for a column space
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       B = response["inputs"]["B"]["matrix"]
#|       A = Matrix([[1, 2, 0], [0, 1, 1], [1, 3, 1]])
#|       right_height = B.rows == A.rows
#|       valid_columns = [
#|           B[:, j] != zeros(B.rows, 1) and A.row_join(B[:, j]).rank() == A.rank()
#|           for j in range(B.cols)
#|       ] if right_height else [False] * B.cols
#|       contained = right_height and all(valid_columns)
#|       independent = right_height and B.rank() == B.cols
#|       complete = independent and B.cols == A.rank()
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(contained) + int(independent) + int(complete)) / 3,
#|           "feedback": "Use nonzero vectors from the column space, keep them independent, and span the complete column space.",
#|           "assessment": {"B": {"columns": valid_columns}}
#|       }

Compute a basis for the column space of
$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0\\0&1&1\\1&3&1\end{bmatrix}$.
Enter your basis vectors as columns of $B$:

$B=$ mat{name=B, rows=3, cols=auto, initial-cols=1, min-cols=0, max-cols=3}
```

## 7. A row-space basis

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-row-space-basis
#| caption: Compute a basis using row vectors
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       R = response["inputs"]["R"]["matrix"]
#|       A = Matrix([[1, 0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 1, 1], [1, 1, 2, 3]])
#|       right_width = R.cols == A.cols
#|       valid_rows = [
#|           R[i, :] != zeros(1, R.cols) and A.col_join(R[i, :]).rank() == A.rank()
#|           for i in range(R.rows)
#|       ] if right_width else [False] * R.rows
#|       contained = right_width and all(valid_rows)
#|       independent = right_width and R.rank() == R.rows
#|       complete = independent and R.rows == A.rank()
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(contained) + int(independent) + int(complete)) / 3,
#|           "feedback": "Each row should be a nonzero row-space vector; the rows must be independent and complete.",
#|           "assessment": {"R": {"rows": valid_rows}}
#|       }

Compute a basis for the row space of
$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&1&2\\0&1&1&1\\1&1&2&3\end{bmatrix}$.
Enter one basis vector per row of $R$:

$R=$ mat{name=R, rows=auto, cols=4, initial-rows=1, min-rows=0, max-rows=3}
```

## 8. Build a 3 × 3 Hessian

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-hessian
#| caption: Notice and repair the initial matrix size
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       H = response["inputs"]["H"]["matrix"]
#|       target = Matrix([[2, 1, 0], [1, 4, 1], [0, 1, 6]])
#|       shape_ok = H.shape == target.shape
#|       valid_rows = [
#|           shape_ok and all(simplify(H[i, j] - target[i, j]) == 0 for j in range(3))
#|           for i in range(H.rows)
#|       ]
#|       row_credit = sum(valid_rows) / 3
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(shape_ok) + row_credit) / 2,
#|           "feedback": "A Hessian has one row and column for every variable; then check each second derivative.",
#|           "assessment": {"H": {"rows": valid_rows}}
#|       }

Find the Hessian of
$f(x,y,z)=x^2+xy+2y^2+yz+3z^2$.
The input deliberately starts too small:

$H_f=$ mat{name=H, rows=auto, cols=auto, initial-rows=2, initial-cols=2, min-rows=1, max-rows=3, min-cols=1, max-cols=3}
```

## 9. Choose a path graph

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-path-adjacency
#| caption: Let the matrix size choose the graph
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       P = response["inputs"]["Pth"]["matrix"]
#|       square = P.rows == P.cols
#|       target = Matrix(P.rows, P.cols, lambda i, j: int(abs(i-j) == 1)) if square else None
#|       valid_rows = [
#|           square and all(simplify(P[i, j] - target[i, j]) == 0 for j in range(P.cols))
#|           for i in range(P.rows)
#|       ]
#|       row_credit = sum(valid_rows) / P.rows if P.rows else 0
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(square) + row_credit) / 2,
#|           "feedback": "A path adjacency matrix is square, has zeros on the diagonal, and joins only consecutive vertices.",
#|           "assessment": {"Pth": {"rows": valid_rows}}
#|       }

Choose between two and five ordered vertices and enter the adjacency matrix of
the path $v_1-v_2-\cdots-v_n$. The size of your matrix chooses $n$:

$P_n=$ mat{name=Pth, rows=auto, cols=auto, initial-rows=2, initial-cols=2, min-rows=2, max-rows=5, min-cols=2, max-cols=5}
```
